doc.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: Handling 'buckets of blood' and Nipsey Russell
summary: Her nervousness in rough clubs, advice from her mother and sister-in-law, and Nipsey Russell as emcee in Brooklyn.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Did you have to learn how to handle yourself with some of the clientele or even some of your fellow musicians, as a young woman. I forgot the name you were calling, you were trying to call some of these clubs.

Well I stayed very uptight. I started off in some very nice ones, but a couple of times some people called, like an emcee, “Ruth come work with me.” And, “Oh my God that’s a ‘bucket of blood.’” So I had this sort of attitude of, you know, very skittish and © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

nervous. And then one night what relaxed me is that I went in one night to a club I did not want to work in. And there was this gorgeous woman at the door collecting money. Elegant, dressed gorgeous, she became one of my best friends. And that relaxed me so I was no longer afraid to work in any bucket of blood. But how I handled myself, I was always a little nervous and a little — you know my mother put the fear of everybody in us you know. Don’t do this, don’t do that. My sister-in-law, who was the exotic dancer, don’t do this, don’t do that, stand this way, blah blah. So I was always a little uptight, but I handled myself very well.
I like your description of a typical act, the full act in a club would consist of an exotic dancer, the singer and the emcee, and a comedian.

No, the emcee was a comedian, the exotic dancer, the singer and of course the house band. And like in Brooklyn when my sister-in-law called me for the Baby Grand in Brooklyn and Nipsey Russell was the emcee.

Yes. And he was quite famous. He was quite famous then, and a wonderful emcee. I was afraid for him to even say boo to me like “hello” — this is Nipsey Russell. So that’s what I mean about being uptight. But my sister-in-law always said, “You don’t do anything but sing for a living, you have a wonderful voice. You sing and don’t take any nonsense from anybody.” And my mother instilled that in me too so I never did. I’d walk out. You’d go to an agent’s office that’s hanky panky, goodbye. You don’t even say goodbye.
